headline: Israel Strikes Lebanon and Gaza as Iran Restricts Strait of Hormuz
subheadline: Hezbollah drone attacks prompt Israeli strikes across southern Lebanon killing 27, while Iran condemns US-Israel attacks on nuclear facilities and announces new maritime restrictions.
lede: Israeli forces struck targets across southern Lebanon and Gaza following Hezbollah drone launches and Hamas operations, killing at least 27 people and injuring 69 over three days. Iran condemned US-Israel attacks on nuclear facilities under IAEA safeguards and announced a new restricted zone beyond the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, despite Putin's order for a three-day pause on Kyiv strikes, Russian Shahed drones and missiles continued hitting multiple Ukrainian districts.

sections.title: Kyiv Hit Despite Putin's Three-Day Ceasefire Order
sections.body: Multiple Shahed drones struck Kyiv districts including Desnianskyi, Pecherskyi, Shevchenkivskyi, Poznyaki, Zhuliany, Teremky, Bortnychi, Brovary, and Boryspil during the declared ceasefire period. Russia deployed eight bombers — four Tu-95MS and four Tu-160 — with Tu-95MS aircraft operating from Olenya airfield. Ukrainian intelligence assesses Russia has sufficient resources to sustain military operations for at least two more years.

sections.title: Israeli Strikes Kill Civilians as Iran Restricts Hormuz
sections.body: Israeli forces launched attacks across southern Lebanon killing civilians including women and children, while IDF struck Hezbollah infrastructure after two drones were launched toward Israeli forces in the security zone. In Gaza, IDF targeted a Hamas terrorist using real-time adjustments to avoid civilian casualties. Iran announced a new restricted zone beyond the Strait of Hormuz, warning vessels against entering.

sections.title: Intelligence Assessment
sections.body: The contradiction between Putin's no-strike order and ongoing drone attacks across multiple Ukrainian oblasts suggests either decentralized command issues or selective targeting restrictions. Iran's restriction of the Strait of Hormuz combined with its condemnation of attacks on nuclear facilities signals potential for further retaliatory escalation in the region.
